originalTitle: Analysis: Why a $2 trillion deficit and 5% Treasury yields are becoming America's biggest economic challenge
summary: Treasury yields above 5% are raising borrowing costs for households and the federal government, highlighting the challenge of financing $2 trillion deficits.
content:
Long-term bond yields above 5% and a $2 trillion deficit are giving Americans a taste of what a U.S. debt crisis would be like. A true emergency would hurt much more, and isn't baked in. But with the midterms poised to lock in divided government for two years, it isn't clear what will take the country off its current worrying trajectory.

Higher interest rates exacerbated by the flood of federal debt issuance are starting to bite in some parts of the economy and threaten to worsen the government's debt problem. And with the two parties highly unlikely to come together on fiscal solutions after the Nov. 3 midterms, any fixes are years off in the future.

The housing market is showing signs of slowing as the average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage hovers around 7.5%. Pending home sales fell 4% in September, Redfin said Monday, the biggest monthly drop in three years.

Mortgage rates track the 10-year Treasury yield . The 10-year has climbed 114 basis points, or hundredths of a percentage point, since the end of February through midday Friday, when the 10-year traded at 5.1%.

Read more CNBC politics and policy coverage

Several factors are pushing up the 10-year, including the war with Iran, which kicked off on Feb. 28 and precipitated the rise in long-term yields. Oil and diesel prices are up sharply, and that has bond traders asking for more yield to account for the possibility that central banks such as the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates.

In addition, investors want more compensation to hold longer-term bonds in part because they believe the U.S. government will continue to flood the market with them. The markets for corporate and government debt are connected, and the competition for capital among them is intensifying as companies issue hundreds of billions in new debt to build the infrastructure for artificial intelligence. Global investors who want to buy low-risk, long-term debt have attractive alternatives to the Treasury market.

If the U.S. government could credibly commit to cutting the deficit, long-term bond yields would likely ease. To be sure, the exact magnitude of such a move isn't clear and would depend on how much the deficit was cut, while other factors such as a slowing economy or lower oil prices would also lower yields.

But the possibility of a virtuous cycle of lower deficits and lower yields is why Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has argued that the U.S. ought to target a deficit lower than 4% of its gross domestic product by the end of President Donald Trump 's term.

There is almost no way the U.S. will hit that target. The deficit was $1.992 trillion for the 2026 fiscal year, up 12% from last year, data released Friday by the U.S. Treasury showed. That deficit amounts to approximately 6.2% of gross domestic product, based on an estimate of third-quarter GDP.

Higher rates make debt reduction tougher. If interest rates stay a half-point above the CBO's expectations, the cumulative deficit over 10 years will come in $1.9 trillion higher, the agency estimates . If rates overshoot by 1.5 points, that adds $6 trillion in deficits.

The CBO expects the 10-year Treasury to average 4.3% over that period, compared with 5.1% today. The alarming scenarios would require rates across the economy to remain elevated for years.

"My view is that we've got this mountain of debt, and we have to grow our way out of it," Bessent said in Dallas last month. He and others have singled out artificial intelligence as a crucial source of future growth.

AI could help but can't fix the problem entirely. It would take a decade of 7.2% growth to balance the budget with growth alone, according to the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget , a research group that advocates for balanced budgets.

GDP growth was recently revised up for the second quarter from 1.5% to 2.2% at an annualized rate. The acceleration that quickly would get us to 7.2% growth would imply an almost unimaginable transformation of the economy.

Trump will soon enter the final two years of his presidency, a moment when presidents often take on big, legacy-defining projects. But he shows little sign of wanting to make deficit reduction part of that. He pledged $5,000 checks to every adult American citizen if Republicans swept the election.

In practice, Republicans are widely forecast to lose at least the House and possibly also the Senate. Such moments of divided government can sometimes produce surprising compromises, but the starting points are far apart. Rep. Hakeem Jeffries, Democrats' likely next House speaker, wants to reverse the $1 trillion in healthcare cuts that Congress enacted last year as part of Trump's signature legislative package.

And that's leaving aside the deep animosity between the parties.

The overall U.S. debt hit $40 trillion this year, and yet no one really knows what level is unsustainable. A full-on debt crisis likely remains much further out in the future. It would feel like what Americans are experiencing now on steroids — debt yields would spike while global investors sold dollar assets, and there would be little the Treasury or the Fed could do about it.

For now, though higher yields are also attracting investors to U.S. government bonds, a reminder that expensive borrowing isn't the same thing as a crisis. But the bottom line is that economics alone can't solve the problem. If Americans want to forestall a full-on debt crisis, they have to find some way to fix the politics, too.
chineseTitle: 分析：为什么2万亿美元的赤字和5%的国债收益率正在成为美国最大的经济挑战
chineseSummary: 超过 5% 的国债收益率正在提高家庭和联邦政府的借贷成本，凸显了为 2 万亿美元赤字融资的挑战。
chineseContent:
超过5%的长期债券收益率和2万亿美元的赤字让美国人尝到了美国债务危机的滋味。真正的紧急情况会造成更大的伤害，而且不会被影响。但由于中期选举准备将分裂的政府锁定两年，目前尚不清楚什么能让该国摆脱目前令人担忧的轨道。

大量联邦债券发行加剧了利率上升，开始对某些经济领域产生影响，并有可能使政府的债务问题恶化。由于两党极不可能在 11 月 3 日中期选举后就财政解决方案达成一致，因此任何解决方案都需要数年时间才能解决。

30 年期固定利率抵押贷款平均利率徘徊在 7.5% 左右，房地产市场显示出放缓迹象。 Redfin 周一表示，9 月份待售房屋销售量下降 4%，创三年来最大单月跌幅。

抵押贷款利率追踪 10 年期国债收益率。自2月底至周五中午，10年期国债已上涨114个基点，即百分之一百分点，当时10年期国债的交易价格为5.1%。

阅读更多 CNBC 政治和政策报道

有几个因素正在推高10年期国债，其中包括2月28日爆发的与伊朗的战争，并加速了长期收益率的上涨。石油和柴油价格大幅上涨，债券交易员要求提高收益率，以考虑美联储等央行加息的可能性。

此外，投资者希望获得更多补偿来持有长期债券，部分原因是他们相信美国政府将继续向市场投放长期债券。企业和政府债务市场相互关联，随着企业发行数千亿新债建设人工智能基础设施，企业之间的资本竞争日益加剧。对于想要购买低风险长期债务的全球投资者来说，除了国债市场之外，还有其他有吸引力的选择。

如果美国政府能够可信地承诺削减赤字，长期债券收益率可能会下降。可以肯定的是，这一举措的具体幅度尚不清楚，将取决于赤字削减的程度，而经济放缓或油价下跌等其他因素也会降低收益率。

但降低赤字和降低收益率的良性循环的可能性正是美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特认为美国应该在唐纳德·特朗普总统任期结束前将赤字目标设定为低于国内生产总值 4% 的原因。

美国几乎不可能实现这一目标。美国财政部周五公布的数据显示，2026财年赤字为1.992万亿美元，比去年增长12%。根据对第三季度 GDP 的估计，该赤字约占国内生产总值的 6.2%。

较高的利率使债务削减变得更加困难。该机构估计，如果利率保持高于国会预算办公室预期半个百分点，10 年内的累计赤字将增加 1.9 万亿美元。如果利率超出 1.5 个百分点，赤字就会增加 6 万亿美元。

美国国会预算办公室预计，同期 10 年期国债利率平均为 4.3%，而目前为 5.1%。令人震惊的情况将要求整个经济体的利率在多年内保持在高位。

贝森特上个月在达拉斯表示：“我的观点是，我们已经背负了如此沉重的债务，我们必须通过发展来摆脱债务。”他和其他人将人工智能视为未来增长的重要来源。

人工智能可以提供帮助，但不能完全解决问题。倡导平衡预算的研究组织负责任的联邦预算委员会表示，需要十年 7.2% 的增长才能实现预算与增长的平衡。

最近，第二季度 GDP 增长率按年率计算从 1.5% 上调至 2.2%。快速加速将使我们的增长率达到 7.2%，这意味着经济将发生几乎难以想象的转变。

特朗普很快将进入总统任期的最后两年，此时总统们经常会承担重大的、定义遗产的项目。但他几乎没有表现出希望将削减赤字纳入其中的迹象。他承诺，如果共和党在选举中获胜，将向每位美国成年公民发放 5,000 美元的支票。

实际上，人们普遍预测共和党将至少失去众议院，甚至可能失去参议院。政府分裂的时刻有时会产生令人惊讶的妥协，但出发点却相差甚远。民主党众议员哈基姆·杰弗里斯（Hakeem Jeffries）可能是下任众议院议长，他希望扭转国会去年颁布的 1 万亿美元医疗保健削减计划，这是特朗普标志性立法计划的一部分。

这还不包括双方之间深深的敌意。

今年美国债务总额达到 40 万亿美元，但没有人真正知道什么水平是不可持续的。全面的债务危机在未来可能还会持续很长时间。这感觉就像美国人现在正在经历的类固醇一样——债务收益率将飙升，而全球投资者出售美元资产，而财政部或美联储对此无能为力。

目前，尽管较高的收益率也吸引了投资者购买美国政府债券，但这提醒人们，昂贵的借贷并不等同于危机。但最重要的是，仅靠经济学无法解决问题。如果美国人想要阻止全面的债务危机，他们也必须找到某种方法来解决政治问题。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
